estimates.t: Management believes that, based on actuarial assumptions and the well-funded status of the pension plan, NEE will not be required to make any cash contributions to the qualified pension plan in the near future.

estimates.name: Nature of Accounting Estimates
estimates.t: The amount of benefit to be paid depends on a number of future events incorporated into the pension benefit formula, including an estimate of the average remaining life of employees/survivors as well as the average years of service rendered.

estimates.name: Table of Content s — Carrying Value of Long-Lived Assets
estimates.t: NEE evaluates long-lived assets for impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount may not be recoverable.

estimates.name: Nature of Accounting Estimates
estimates.t: The amount of future net cash flows, the timing of the cash flows and the determination of an appropriate interest rate all involve estimates and judgments about future events.

estimates.name: Assumptions and Accounting Approach
estimates.t: In most instances, the fair value is determined by discounting estimated future cash flows using an appropriate interest rate.

estimates.name: Carrying Value of Equity Method Investments
estimates.t: NEE tests its equity method investments for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the fair value of the investment is less than the carrying value .

estimates.name: Nature of Accounting Estimates
estimates.t: If indicators of impairment exist, an estimate of the investment’s fair value will be calculated.

estimates.name: Assumptions and Accounting Approach
estimates.t: Investments that are other than temporarily impaired are written down to their estimated fair value and cannot subsequently be written back up for increases in estimated fair value.
